label: fable-RAW
text:
VERDICT: HOLD

FINDINGS:
1. [severity: high] src/components/desktop/thoughts/useOrchestratorStream.ts — The entire metered-compaction feature hinges on `data.backend` arriving on ws events, but no ws-server change is in this batch (the socket tests fabricate the field; comments merely assert "rides every emission"). If the server doesn't stamp it, `lastBackendRef` stays null and a Fable session silently compacts at the global 300K threshold — per-token re-reads of a ~300K window every turn, the exact billing failure this feature exists to prevent, failing open with no error.
2. [severity: high] src/components/desktop/thoughts/use-orchestrator-stream/shared.ts — The metered reset floor (12,000) exactly equals `ORCHESTRATOR_SYSTEM_PROMPT_ESTIMATE_TOKENS` (4,000) + `ORCHESTRATOR_NEXT_TURN_BUFFER_TOKENS` (8,000); if `runningTotal` includes those estimates, a post-compaction total can never fall strictly below the floor, `autoCompactArmedRef` never re-arms, and the session gets exactly one auto-compact ever, then grows unbounded on metered billing. A reviewer must verify what `runningTotal` actually comprises.
3. [severity: high] src/lib/orchestrator/brain-access.ts — `resolvePacketBrainEnabled` keys the Brain flip on the *operator-default* backend, but active-backend.ts itself documents that a per-request `msg.backend` override wins at the ws layer; a session actually running Fable while the default is codex gets no Brain flip (workers route questions back through the metered window), and conversely default=fable flips the Brain on for dispatches from every backend.
4. [severity: med] src/lib/lane/orchestrator-session.ts — `isFable` takes precedence over `permissionMode === 'plan'`: a Fable turn requested in plan mode silently runs with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` plus live operator dispatch tools, dropping plan mode's no-mutation guarantee without surfacing it. Documented as deliberate, but it's a permission downgrade a caller won't expect.
5. [severity: med] src/lib/lane/orchestrator-backends/fable-config.ts — When `O8_FABLE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset, `fableEnvOverride()` returns `{}` and the Fable proc silently runs on ambient credentials — i.e., the subscription pool absorbs metered-class Fable traffic (or the spawn fails obscurely if Fable-5 isn't on the plan). No fail-loud path; the cross-billing guard is one-directional.
6. [severity: med] src/components/desktop/thoughts/use-orchestrator-stream/socket.ts — `lastBackendRef` is stamped from *any* orchestrator event including replays, snapshots, and per-request-override turns, so one overridden codex turn flips the whole session's compaction thresholds back to 300K until the next fable-stamped event; and because it's a ref (not state), a backend-only event doesn't re-run the compaction effect — the new threshold applies only after the next `runningTotal`/`status` change.
7. [severity: med] src/lib/mcp/operator-handlers/digest.ts — `handleFetchRaw` records a rate-limit slot *before* delegating, so malformed calls or failed transcript reads (bad packetId) permanently burn the 5-per-10-min budget; and the limiter's "per session" claim depends on the operator MCP server actually being one proc per session — if the proc is shared, sessions starve each other, and a proc restart silently resets the meter.
8. [severity: med] src/lib/lane/orchestrator-backends/fable.ts — `void prewarmHaiku()` / `void prewarmSonnetCli()` discard the promises without `.catch`; a rejection (e.g., CLI missing, network) becomes an unhandled rejection, which can terminate the node process under default modern Node settings — a prewarm nicety that can kill the orchestrator host.
9. [severity: low] src/lib/lane/fable-profile.ts — Under `--strict-mcp-config` the four `mcp__o8__*` / defense-in-depth deny names match no known tool, emitting on every spawn the exact "matches no known tool" warning the `MultiEdit` omission was crafted to avoid; and the `mcp__operator__*` / `mcp__cortex__*` wire names silently couple to the server keys emitted by build.ts — a rename there reopens the raw-transcript hole with no test tying the two together.
10. [severity: low] src/lib/tiles/operations.ts — The terminal↔terminal collapse discards `children[1]` entirely (any per-leaf state on the second terminal is silently lost) and only matches exactly-2-child splits, so any other stale terminal-split shape still renders duplicated surfaces.

MISSED-BY-TESTS:
1. Nothing tests the auto-compact effect's actual wiring: no test sets `lastBackendRef` to 'fable' with `runningTotal` between 15K and 300K and asserts compaction fires (and doesn't for a subscription backend). The constants exist and the ref-stamping is tested, but the decision logic in `useOrchestratorStream` — the feature's core — is uncovered, as is the server-side emission of `data.backend` it depends on.
2. No test covers re-arm after a metered compaction — that a compaction actually lands below the 12K floor and the trigger re-arms. A hysteresis deadlock (finding 2) would pass this entire suite green.
3. Only `fableLockoutArgs()` is unit-tested; no test drives `spawnOrchestratorProc` with `toolProfile: 'fable'` to assert the spawned argv actually contains the lockout flags and the env actually carries the BYO key — the branch in orchestrator-session.ts that makes Layer B real is uncovered (the same isolation-test trap the batch's own seam-D comment warns about).

ASSESSMENT: This is a thoughtfully layered change — billing-class abstraction instead of name-matching, fail-closed Codex guard, separate MCP config files to avoid clobber races, strict-mcp-config after a live dogfood hole, and honest empirical notes throughout — but the highest-stakes path ships on faith. The metered compaction trigger, the single mechanism protecting a per-token window from growing 20× past its target, is client-side logic keyed to a server field this batch never adds, fails open to the expensive 300K behavior when that field is absent, and carries an exact-sum floor (12K = 4K + 8K) that plausibly disarms it permanently after one firing — and none of the three is exercised by a test. Add to that the operator-default vs. per-request-override mismatch in the Brain flip and the silent subscription fallback when the BYO key is unset, and the batch's billing guarantees are weaker than its comments claim. Hold until the ws-server backend emission is confirmed in-tree, the `runningTotal` floor reachability is verified or the floor lowered, and at least one test drives the compaction decision and the fable spawn end-to-end; everything else here is shippable as-is.

label: fable-WINDOW
text:
VERDICT: HOLD

FINDINGS:
1. [severity: high] src/lib/lane/orchestrator-backends/fable.ts — The two load-bearing invariants (tool lockout args, BYO-key env override) are applied at **spawn**, but the model/toolProfile override is applied per-**turn**, and `ensureOrchestratorSession(repoPath, threadId)` is keyed by repo/thread, not backend. Flip the operator default from `claude` to `fable` mid-session and the existing REPL proc — spawned with full native tools and ambient subscription credentials — is reused to run claude-fable-5: metered model, no lockout, wrong billing identity.
2. [severity: high] src/lib/lane/fable-profile.ts — The lockout is a *denylist* combined with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`: every native tool not explicitly listed is auto-approved. Anything the list misses (e.g. `MultiEdit`, `NotebookRead`, `LS`, or any tool added in a future CLI release) silently gives the metered model a bulk-read path. A decisions-only sandbox should be an allowlist; a denylist decays with every CLI upgrade. Separately verify that `--disallowedTools` followed by spread tool names parses as variadic in the real CLI and that nothing appended after it in the spawn argv gets swallowed as a "tool name".
3. [severity: high] src/components/desktop/thoughts/useOrchestratorStream.ts — The metered auto-compact ceiling lives entirely in a browser React effect. o8 governs *autonomous* fleets; a lane running with no panel open (or a backgrounded tab with throttled effects) never compacts, and the per-token-metered orchestrator accumulates context without bound. The cost ceiling for a metered backend must be enforced server-side.
4. [severity: high] src/lib/lane/orchestrator-backends/fable-config.ts — Nothing described hard-fails when `O8_FABLE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset: `fableEnvOverride()` maps the BYO key when present, but when absent the fable proc inherits ambient credentials and claude-fable-5 runs on the operator's subscription/ambient key silently — the inverse of the "BYO must never leak into subscription procs" constraint, and the more expensive failure mode.
5. [severity: med] src/components/desktop/thoughts/use-orchestrator-stream/socket.ts — `lastBackendRef` is stamped from `data.backend` **before** seq dedup, so a late/replayed event from a prior non-fable turn (or another lane if the socket multiplexes) regresses the ref and the compact effect silently reverts to the 300K global threshold on a metered lane. It's also `null` until the first event, so the first stretch of a fable session runs under the global threshold.
6. [severity: med] src/components/desktop/thoughts/use-orchestrator-stream/shared.ts — The metered band is threshold 15,000 / re-arm floor 12,000. If a post-compaction transcript (summary + system prompt + Brain block) lands ≥12K — quite plausible — `autoCompactArmedRef` never re-arms and compaction fires exactly once per session, after which the metered window grows unchecked. Verify a realistic post-compact size against the 12K floor.
7. [severity: med] src/lib/mcp/operator-handlers/digest.ts — `fetch_raw` is rate-limited by call **count** but not output **size**: one allowed call can pull an arbitrarily large raw transcript straight into the metered model's window, blowing past the 15K compact target in a single tool result. The limiter is also module-level state per MCP proc, so it resets on proc respawn/compaction restart; and the companion `digest` tool has no rate limit at all while spawning a fresh Codex exec per call.
8. [severity: med] src/lib/tiles/operations.ts — Unrelated to Fable mode: `migrateNode` collapsing a persisted split whose two children are terminal leaves by "returning first child" discards the second leaf. If two distinct leaf panes can both be terminal, this is silent user-layout data loss riding in a high-stakes batch; at minimum it should ship separately.
9. [severity: med] src/lib/lane/orchestrator-backends/registry.ts — `isMeteredOrchestratorBackend` is re-exported from registry.ts, which imports fable.ts → orchestrator-session (server-only). If useOrchestratorStream imports the predicate via the registry re-export instead of the billing.ts leaf, server code lands in the client bundle — the exact hazard the "billing.ts must stay client-bundle-safe" constraint exists for. Verify the hook's actual import path.
10. [severity: low] src/lib/orchestrator/brain-access.ts — Precedence subtlety: `mode === 'off'` beats the metered check, which honors the stated constraint but means an operator with `workersUseBrain: off` gets a fable orchestrator that can't read raw transcripts *and* workers without the Brain — the mode's compensating mechanism silently disabled. Also, only the production entry passes `orchestratorBackend`; every other caller of `resolveBrainEnabledWith` gets pre-batch semantics, so audit call sites.

MISSED-BY-TESTS:
1. Backend switching mid-session: no test flips `claude` → `fable` (or back) on a live thread and asserts the reused/respawned proc carries the lockout args, BYO env, and correct billing identity — the finding-1 seam is entirely untested.
2. End-to-end lockout enforcement: fable-profile.test.ts asserts the *arrays/args*, but nothing spawns the real CLI and confirms `--disallowedTools` variadic parsing actually blocks Read/Bash/mcp raw tools (or that `--strict-mcp-config` plus profile stripping interact as intended).
3. The missing-BYO-key path and the headless-lane path: no test asserts fable refuses (or warns) without `O8_FABLE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and no test exercises token growth on a lane with no connected panel, where the client-side compact effect never runs.

ASSESSMENT: The design intent is coherent — one metered decision-maker, bulk pushed to digests, Brain moved to workers — and the pure-leaf billing module, the explicit-setting precedence in brain-access, and the digest/fetch_raw metering line show real care. But the batch enforces its two most expensive invariants at the wrong layer: tool lockout and BYO billing are spawn-time properties of a session that is selected and reused per-turn by backend-agnostic keys, and the cost ceiling for the only per-token-metered model in the system is a browser useEffect with a re-arm band narrow enough to jam after one firing. Combined with a denylist-under-skip-permissions sandbox that decays with CLI upgrades, a fetch_raw escape hatch capped by count but not bytes, and an unrelated persisted-layout migration with data-loss potential riding along, this is not shippable as-is. Fix the session-reuse seam, hard-fail on a missing BYO key, move (or mirror) the compact trigger server-side, and split out the tiles migration; the rest is polish.

label: opus-RAW
text:
VERDICT: HOLD

FINDINGS:
1. [high] src/components/desktop/thoughts/use-orchestrator-stream/socket.ts — Backend is stamped into `lastBackendRef` on *every* event carrying `data.backend`, deliberately *before* seq-dedup/snapshot gating and with last-write-wins. A single stale/replayed event from a different session (or any emission where `backend` is momentarily not `'fable'`) flips the ref off `'fable'`, so the client auto-compact effect reverts to the 300K global threshold and the metered window grows unbounded — a direct per-token billing blowout on the one backend that is actually metered. The test even codifies `fable`→`codex` flipping on a deduped replay as correct.

2. [high] src/lib/orchestrator/auto-compact.ts — `DIGEST_INPUT_CHAR_CAP = 180_000` is described as an "argv-safety cap … the prompt rides as a single codex argv element," but Linux caps a single argv string at `MAX_ARG_STRLEN` = 128 KiB (131072 bytes). A near-cap digest (128K–180K chars) exceeds that and the codex `exec` fails with E2BIG on Linux; the cap only "works" on the darwin dev box. Cap must be < ~120K or the payload must go via stdin/temp file.

3. [high] src/lib/lane/fable-profile.ts / fable-config.ts — `fableEnvOverride()` returns `{}` when `O8_FABLE_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is unset, so a Fable turn then spawns with the ambient `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from `process.env`. There is no guard requiring the BYO key: all metered policies (native-tool lockout, 15K compaction, Brain-always-on) still apply, but billing silently lands on the ambient/subscription credential — the exact policy↔billing mismatch Fable exists to prevent. Fable should fail closed (or refuse to spawn) when no BYO key is resolved.

4. [med] src/lib/orchestrator/brain-access.ts — `resolvePacketBrainEnabled` reads metered-ness from `resolveOrchestratorBackendId()` (the *operator-default* backend), but the comment in active-backend.ts states a per-request `msg.backend` still overrides that setting for the actual turn. So operator=`codex` + per-request `fable` → Brain flip *does not* fire though the real orchestrator is metered; operator=`fable` + per-request override → Brain flips wrongly. The dispatch-time Brain decision can disagree with the backend actually running the turn.

5. [med] src/components/desktop/thoughts/useOrchestratorStream.ts — Metered re-arm gap is only 3K (floor 12K vs threshold 15K), and the system-prompt estimate alone is 4K. `autoCompactArmedRef` only re-arms when `runningTotal < 12K`; if a compacted metered window ever settles at 12–15K (summary + retained recent turn), auto-compaction disarms permanently for the rest of the session and the window drifts up to the 850K force-compact — silent loss of the metered discipline. Needs proof that compaction reliably lands < 12K.

6. [med] src/lib/mcp/operator-handlers/digest.ts — The `fetch_raw` limiter is module-global (`fetchRawCallsAt`), and its correctness claim ("per MCP-server proc = per orchestrator session") is load-bearing and unverified. If one operator-mcp-server process serves multiple repos/sessions, the 5-per-10-min budget is shared across all of them and one session starves another; if it's genuinely per-proc, confirm that invariant explicitly.

7. [med] src/lib/lane/orchestrator-session.ts — In `spawnOrchestratorProc`, `isFable` takes precedence over the `permissionMode === 'plan'` branch, so a Fable turn requested in plan mode silently spawns with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` instead of `--permission-mode plan`. A caller expecting plan-mode (dry-run) semantics gets an autonomous turn with no signal; verify no path can request Fable + plan.

8. [low] src/components/desktop/thoughts/useOrchestratorStream.ts — The effect reads `lastBackendRef.current` (a ref, not in the dep array). On the first turn, before any backend-bearing event lands, `metered` is false and the global 300K threshold applies; the metered threshold only engages on the next `runningTotal`/`status` re-render. A fast opening turn could briefly exceed 15K before metered gating kicks in.

9. [low] src/lib/operator/defaults.ts — `ORCHESTRATOR_MODEL_OPTIONS` drops `claude-sonnet-4-6` for `claude-sonnet-5` (a drive-by unrelated to Fable). An operator with `claude-sonnet-4-6` persisted keeps a value no longer offered in the dropdown; confirm `resolveOrchestratorModelSync` still accepts the retired id and the UI doesn't blank the selection.

10. [low] src/lib/tiles/operations.ts — The terminal↔terminal collapse returns `node.children[0]` and silently discards `children[1]`; any per-leaf persisted terminal state/id on the dropped leaf is lost. Intended for the two-full-terminals bug, but confirm nothing keyed off the second leaf's id survives elsewhere in the persisted layout.

MISSED-BY-TESTS:
1. No test drives the client auto-compact effect end-to-end: that `lastBackendRef==='fable'` actually selects the 15K threshold, that a non-fable event reverts it, or that the 12K/15K re-arm doesn't starve after a real compaction. socket.test only asserts the ref is stamped, not that it changes compaction behavior — the same isolation trap the seam-D comment warns about, left open on the highest-risk path.
2. No test exercises the real spawn path (`spawnOrchestratorProc`) wiring `isFable`: that `fableLockoutArgs()`/`fableEnvOverride()` actually reach `spawn`, that `--strict-mcp-config` + `-fable` config coexist, or that isFable overrides plan mode. fable-profile.test only checks the arg-builder in isolation; the empirical "deny fires under skip-permissions" claim is asserted nowhere in CI.
3. Nothing covers the billing-critical edge cases: Fable spawned with no BYO key (ambient fallback), the per-request `msg.backend` override vs brain-access divergence, or the digest argv cap against a real codex exec (the 180K/128K limit).

ASSESSMENT: The architecture is clean — billing class as the single keying axis, pure/server leaf split, fail-closed on the Codex mis-wire, and thorough comments — and most of the batch is defensible. But three issues are ship-blocking for a *metered* backend where the failure mode is money: backend tracking that lets a stray replayed event silently disable metered compaction, a digest argv cap that exceeds Linux's per-arg limit, and a BYO-key path that silently falls back to ambient billing with no guard. Each converts a "policy applied" appearance into wrong-pool billing or unbounded token spend, and none is covered by the described tests, whose weight sits on isolated arg-builders and the rate limiter rather than the load-bearing client-compaction and spawn seams. Hold until #1–#3 are fixed and the metered-compaction/spawn paths get real end-to-end coverage.

label: opus-WINDOW
text:
VERDICT: HOLD

FINDINGS:
1. [high] fable.ts / orchestrator-session.ts — `sendTurn` calls `ensureOrchestratorSession`, which reuses an existing claude REPL proc; but `fableLockoutArgs()` and `fableEnvOverride()` are applied only at *spawn*. Switching a repo that already has a live subscription-billed claude session to fable would run the metered model on a proc with native tools NOT stripped and the BYO key NOT applied — violating both the tool-lockout and the billing guard. Verify fable never delegates over a pre-existing non-fable session.
2. [high] useOrchestratorStream.ts — metered threshold 15k / reset floor 12k. Re-arming requires `runningTotal < 12_000` after a compaction; if the aggressive-but-nonzero compacted context can't fall below 12k, `autoCompactArmedRef` never re-arms, auto-compact fires exactly once, and the metered model then runs unbounded. The 3k arm/fire band is dangerously tight for a per-token-metered loop.
3. [high] socket.ts — `lastBackendRef` is stamped from `data.backend` on *every* WS event *before* seq dedup. If any event (including a replayed/duplicate one, or one lacking `backend`) assigns `undefined`/a non-metered id, `metered` flips false and the hook silently uses the 300k global threshold on a metered session — a ~20x budget overrun before compaction. Verify it only ever writes valid metered ids and never regresses to null.
4. [high] operator-handlers/digest.ts — `fetch_raw` is the one bulk-escape hatch and is only *rate*-limited (5/10min), not *size*-limited; it delegates to `handleTranscript` and appends a meter line, but if the transcript payload itself is uncapped the metered model absorbs full raw bulk, defeating the batch's whole premise. Also the counter is per-MCP-proc module state, so a reconnect/respawn resets it.
5. [high] billing.ts / registry.ts — the React hook imports `isMeteredOrchestratorBackend`/`isOrchestratorBackendId`. If those resolve through `registry.ts` (which registers/imports the fable backend and its server deps) rather than the pure `billing.ts` leaf, server-only code is dragged into the client bundle. Confirm the hook's import path terminates at the leaf.
6. [med] fable-profile.ts — the entire native-tool lockout rests on `--disallowedTools` being (a) not overridden by the co-passed `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, (b) variadic enough to consume the concatenated tool+MCP list as one flag, and (c) honoring wildcard `mcp__o8__*` matching. If wildcards aren't matched by the CLI, the raw-transcript MCP aliases are not actually denied.
7. [med] brain-access.ts — the metered→Brain flip is gated on the *optional* `orchestratorBackend` param; precedence over `mode==='off'` and `useBrain:false` is correctly honored (both return before the metered branch), but any production/non-production call-site that forgets to thread the backend silently drops workers back to the tier default. Coverage is only as good as every call-site.
8. [med] tiles/operations.ts — `migrateNode` collapsing a persisted split whose two children are both terminal leaves to "return first child" discards the second leaf's content (layout data loss), and this is unrelated scope bundled into a high-stakes billing batch — it should not ship on this branch.
9. [med] fable.ts — `prewarmHaiku()`/`prewarmSonnetCli()` fire on every `sendTurn`; verify these ambient/subscription prewarm procs cannot inherit the fable `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (BYO-key leak into subscription billing) and that per-turn re-spawns are idempotent rather than accumulating procs.
10. [low] fable-config.ts / active-backend.ts — model + BYO key are re-read each call and `resolveOrchestratorBackendId` was moved and re-exported; verify there is one authoritative resolver (no divergence between active-backend.ts and the registry re-export) and that a mid-session env change can't produce a `model` inconsistent with the already-spawned proc.

MISSED-BY-TESTS:
1. No test exercises the compaction *re-arm* path — that a metered session, after auto-compacting, actually drops below the 12k reset floor and can fire again; the runaway-spend scenario in finding #2 is untested.
2. No test covers fable delegating over a *pre-existing* orchestrator session (finding #1) — the lockout/BYO tests presumably assert on fresh-spawn args, not the reuse case where the guards are absent.
3. `digest.test.ts` covers rate-limit paths but not `fetch_raw` output *size* bounding, nor prewarm procs inheriting the BYO key — the two ways the "never absorb bulk / no key leak" invariants can still break.

ASSESSMENT: The batch is architecturally coherent and the visible precedence seams (brain-access honoring explicit off before the metered flip; fable.ts forcing model/toolProfile after caller options) are correct, but for a per-token-metered model the load-bearing guarantees live in exactly the spots the digest leaves unproven: whether the lockout and BYO-key env survive session reuse, whether the metered auto-compact loop can actually re-arm, whether the backend-tracking ref can regress and silently reinstate the 300k threshold, and whether the fetch_raw escape hatch is size-bounded rather than merely rate-limited. Any one of the four high findings is a real billing or bulk-absorption breach, and none is covered by the eleven new tests; the unrelated tile-migration change is also a gratuitous data-loss risk that doesn't belong here. This should not ship until findings 1–5 are verified against the actual code (not the digest) and the re-arm/session-reuse/fetch_raw-size gaps get tests — HOLD.
